newsitem.title: ITALY: Rail travel in Italy hit by week of protests.
newsitem.headline: Rail travel in Italy hit by week of protests.

text.p: Train travellers in Italy were told on Monday to expect a week of delays after railway employees called a series of protests to press their demand for a safety review following a fatal train derailment.

The first of three separate actions was to begin on Monday afternoon by train drivers whose union has ordered them to keep to speeds below the limits set out for various sections of track and not to exceed 150 kph (95 mph).

The COMU drivers' union, one of several in the industry, said the go-slow would continue until the state railway company, Ferrovie dello Stato (FS), had met union demands for a joint review of safety systems, track maintenance and working hours.

Railroad unions have been asking for more stringent safety measures since January 12 when eight people were killed and another 30 injured after a Milan-Rome high-speed "Pendolino" train derailed near the northern city of Piacenza.
The union representing railway station workers, who control the flow of train traffic, have called a 48 hour strike starting from 2000 GMT on Tuesday.
A third protest was set to begin on Wednesday when railway workers from the independent Fisat-Cisa union would seek to delay the departure of trains by one hour for a week.

FS managing director Giancarlo Cimoli said last week that there was no immediate evidence that the train, built to tilt into bends at speed, had been faulty or that the track on which it was travelling had been defective.
He added, however, that rail safety would be looked at closely.
Authorities have focused on speed as a possible cause for the derailment of the train, Italy's fastest.
Futher travel problems were reported on Monday at Milan's Linate Airport where dairy farmers continued to demonstrate against European Union milk quotes for a fourth day.
The dairy farmers, who had been blocking the airport's access roads forcing passengers to walk kilometres (miles), eased the blockade on Monday allowing private cars to pass by to reach the terminal.
